author: Lucy Campbell
description:
David Rush accused of stealing hundreds of gold bars worth over $40m and hiding them in his basement

Federal prosecutors have reached a tentative plea agreement with a former CIA officer accused of stealing hundreds of gold bars worth more than $40m from the US spy agency and hiding them in his basement, court records show.

David Rush and federal justice department prosecutors have a “plea agreement in principle”, the parties said in a Friday court filing. The parties also asked a judge to extend the 17 September deadline for three weeks through 8 October to allow them time to “resolve the matter prior to an indictment”.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars reaches tentative plea deal

author: Associated Press
description:
The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks

Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.

The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.
title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11

author: Maya Yang
description:
The disease is a form of pneumonia caused by Legionella bacteria, which can grow in warm water and spread through mist produced by cooling towers

One person has died from legionnaires’ disease, and four more have been sickened in New York City amid a new cluster of cases only weeks after local health officials had declared a separate deadly Manhattan outbreak of the illness over.

On Thursday, New York City officials announced that their municipal health department launched an investigation into a community cluster in parts of Melrose and Morrisania in the South Bronx, including ZIP codes 10451 and 10456.

Continue reading...
title: Legionnaires’ disease outbreak kills one and infects others in the South Bronx

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Prosecutors say James Brass orchestrated scheme to pay people on LA’s Skid Row to duplicate registered voters’ signatures

A California ballot petition worker has been arrested and charged with identity fraud for allegedly paying people on Los Angeles’ Skid Row to forge the signatures of registered voters.

Prosecutors say James Brass, 47, orchestrated the scheme with the help of two signature collectors, 49-year-old Courtney Price and 33-year-old Jateisha Herron.

Continue reading...
title: California petition worker arrested for allegedly paying people to forge voter signs

author: Rowena Mason
description:
Ben Delo was convicted in US for failing to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls but pardoned by Trump

Reform has been given a record £36m donation by Ben Delo, a British cryptocurrency billionaire convicted in the US for failing to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls.

The businessman, who has moved back to the UK from Hong Kong, is now the biggest UK political donor by far, dwarfing the £15m contribution to Reform UK from Thailand-based donor Christopher Harborne.

Continue reading...
title: Reform UK given record £36m donation by British crypto billionaire

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Nekime Matu Oxendine accused of first-degree murder of Adam Bean, shot and killed in apparent domestic dispute

A North Carolina state highway patrol trooper has been charged with the murder of the captain of a county sheriff’s office.

Cumberland county Capt Adam Bean was shot and killed on 27 March at a home in the town of Hope Mills. A grand jury on Tuesday indicted Nekime Matu Oxendine, 44, with first-degree murder in Bean’s death, and a judge ordered him held without bond pending the outcome of the case.

Continue reading...
title: North Carolina state trooper charged with murder of police captain

author: Roque Planas
description:
The wild feline made its home in the park before being euthanized in 2022 after showing signs of declining health

The city of Los Angeles will memorialize its most famous mountain lion with a bronze sculpture at Griffith Park, the 4,200-acre (1,700-hectare) stretch of land the cougar once roamed.

Known as “P-22”, the number assigned by the team of biologists that first identified him, the lion gained national fame after photographer Steve Winter captured an iconic image of him prowling through Griffith Park with the Hollywood sign in the background.

Continue reading...
title: Los Angeles to memorialize late mountain lion P-22 with sculpture in Griffith Park

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Atlantic Industrial Coatings was given $14.7m no-bid contract and its findings contradict president’s claims of vandalism

The company hired to renovate the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool has acknowledged that “human oversight” and flaws in the repair plan caused the newly installed blue liner to peel and tear, according to documents reviewed by the New York Times that challenge Donald Trump’s repeated claims of vandalism.

The president has repeatedly said vandals armed with knives or box cutters were responsible for tearing apart the pool’s “American flag blue” liner. But documents reviewed by the Times show that Atlantic Industrial Coatings, the company awarded the renovation contract, blamed its own execution of the repair work and a flawed design plan.
title: Company hired for Trump’s reflecting pool makeover reportedly admits flaws in plan

author: Reuters
description:
Democratic attorney general seeks damages and penalties in legal action that echoes thousands of similar suits

Arizona has sued L’Oréal that the French cosmetics company hid evidence that its hair relaxer products ⁠could cause cancer in women – echoing thousands of similar lawsuits from users and their families.

Arizona attorney general Kristin Mayes, a ⁠Democrat, filed the lawsuit late ⁠on Thursday in ​state court. The lawsuit makes Arizona the first state to sue over alleged cancer risks linked to hair relaxers. It also alleges that L’Oréal is violating ⁠state consumer protection laws by marketing the hair relaxer products that are used predominantly by African American women without warning consumers about the alleged risks of ovarian and uterine c
title: Arizona accuses L’Oréal of concealing cancer risks linked to hair relaxers

author: Associated Press
description:
A federal court is declaring that the energy department exceeded its authority when it forced a Michigan power plant to stay open past its scheduled retirement date

In a defeat for the Trump administration, a federal court on Friday ruled that the energy department exceeded its authority when it forced a Michigan coal-fired power plant to stay open past its scheduled retirement date last year.

Energy secretary Chris Wright had said the 64-year-old JH Campbell Generating Plant was needed to ensure reliable electricity in the region, and he used emergency powers to keep it operating. Environmental groups and three states – Michigan, Illinois and Minnesota – went to court to try to overturn orders keeping the plant online.

Continue reading...
title: Federal court rejects Trump order keeping Michigan coal plant open

author: Reuters
description:
Stephen Aarons said he tried to use ChatGPT to create a ‘bulletproof summary’ during a murder conviction appeal

A defense lawyer appealing his client’s murder conviction submitted a legal brief containing ⁠made-up police testimony and ⁠witnesses fabricated by OpenAI’s ChatGPT, ​New Mexico’s highest court said.

The New Mexico supreme court on Wednesday fined the attorney, Stephen Aarons, and held him in contempt for failing to verify the accuracy of the court ⁠filing, which Aarons said he prepared with help from the artificial intelligence (AI) application.

Continue reading...
title: New Mexico lawyer fined for using AI-generated brief containing fabricated police testimony

author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
description:
DUP education minister accused of dragging feet before revising guidelines that also apply to PE and games

Schools in Northern Ireland must give girls the choice to wear trousers as part of their uniforms as well as for PE and games, according to revised guidelines.

From next year schools will no longer be able to prohibit female pupils from wearing trousers, Paul Givan, the country’s education minister, said on Friday. “Today, I am taking that decision, that will be formally communicated, schools will be hearing from me,” he told the BBC.

Continue reading...
title: Northern Ireland schools must give girls option to wear trousers from next year

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
MPs quietly withdrew support when it became clear it was not a priority of Andy Burnham’s government

After two years of impassioned arguments, tearful personal testimonies, noisy protests and ethical dilemmas, the assisted dying bill for England and Wales failed on a knife edge.

Campaigners on the pro side largely blame the House of Lords for making it seem an impossible struggle to get the bill through parliament, after blocking it the first time by putting through more than 1,000 amendments so that it ran out of time.

Continue reading...
title: Why did the assisted dying bill fail in the Commons? | Rowena Mason

author: Shrai Popat and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
The president and the defense secretary tried to link the worst terrorist attack in US history to the unpopular war

  • US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth used remarks at memorial marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11 to defend the US-Israel war on Iran – and suggest the controversial conflict was part of the legacy of the worst terrorist attack in US history.

While such ceremonies on September 11 typically focus on the victims of the 2001 attacks, the US president and his defense secretary each pointed to the war they launched on Iran more than six months ago, with no end in
title: Trump and Hegseth use 9/11 memorial remarks at Pentagon to defend war on Iran

author: Lauren Aratani
description:
Price for the crop dropped dramatically this summer after the cyclospora outbreak caused demand to wilt

At the Republicans’ midterm convention held earlier this week, Donald Trump said that “food prices and almost every other item are rapidly going down”. Fresh inflation data on Friday told a different story – but in one specific case, costs have been chopped.

The price of lettuce dropped dramatically this summer after the cyclospora outbreak caused demand to wilt, with prices dropping even further in August, according to new data released on Friday.

Continue reading...
title: US lettuce prices chopped as costs for other goods remain stubbornly high

author: Rowena Mason and Kiran Stacey
description:
Greens accuse Labour of hiding approval recommendation to avoid controversy ahead of key ballot

A decision on approving the controversial Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea is to be delayed until later this autumn, with the Greens accusing Labour of hiding their position before the crucial Holborn byelection.

Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, had been poised to give her recommendation to approve the Jackdaw field off the coast of Aberdeen next week.

Continue reading...
title: North Sea gasfield decision likely delayed until after Holborn byelection

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Exclusive: FoI documents show senior health officials were warned of concerns about assessment tool weeks after it launched

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

People with dementia were warned not to apply for home support because of fears their care would be downgraded by the government’s aged care algorithm.

Documents released to Guardian Australia under freedom of information (FoI) laws reveal the warnings came within weeks of the November rollout of the algorithm, which is used to determine funding packages and priority of need for older Australians requiring home support.
title: Dementia patients warned off seeking home care in case Australia’s aged care algorithm cuts funding

author: Lisa Cox Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Federal environment department tells industry representatives the government does not want to ‘exacerbate cost of living pressures’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Albanese government has been accused of breaking a promise after it shelved a longstanding commitment to bring in packaging standards intended to force manufacturers and retailers to cut plastic waste.

The federal environment department told industry representatives via email last week that the promise would not be kept before the next election because the government did not want to “exacerbate cost of livin
title: Labor ditches new packaging laws to cut plastic waste, sparking unprecedented ‘scale and breadth of outrage’

author: Oliver Milman
description:
The 23ft-long trackway, consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right, date from 66.5m years ago

The first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex has been found in North Dakota by a team of scientists.

The 23ft-long trackway – consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right – was first identified in the south-west of the state, in the dinosaur fossil area known as Hell Creek Formation, last year by researchers from the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado and Liverpool John Moores University in the UK.

Continue reading...
title: One giant step: first known T rex footprints found in North Dakota

author: Seán Clarke
description:
MPs today voted not to approve the assisted dying bill at its second reading. The bill, which was brought back to the Commons after being blocked in the Lords, would have allowed terminally ill people to end their lives with medical help in some circumstances. Find out how your MP voted

Continue reading...
title: How did your MP vote on the reintroduced assisted dying bill?

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
Annualized inflation rate was 3.4%, same as July, and core inflation, which omits energy and food prices, was up to 2.4%

US consumer prices remained stubbornly high in August as the end of the ceasefire between the US and Iran pushed energy prices up, according to data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics released on Friday.

The annualized inflation rate was 3.4%, the same as it was in July. The most recent peak was seen in May, when the inflation rate hit a three-year high at 4.2%. Core inflation, which strips out volatile energy and food prices, increased to 2.4% in August.

Continue reading...
title: US consumer prices stayed high in August as Iran war pushed energy costs up

author: Amy Hawkins in Kyiv
description:
Three facilities in two days struck as bombardment of Ukraine’s capital enters new phase of intensity

  • Europe live – latest updates

Petrol stations in Kyiv have been hit by jet-powered drones in a wave of targeted Russian attacks as the bombardment of Ukraine’s capital enters a new phase of intensity.

At least two people were killed and six injured in strikes on two petrol stations on Friday morning, according to the city’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko.

Continue reading...
title: Russia targets Kyiv petrol stations for first time with jet-powered drones

author: Martin Belam
description:
Commemoration ceremonies to be held around the world for the nearly 3,000 killed in 2001 terror attack on US. Plus, JD Vance sets out his stall as heir to Donald Trump

Good morning. It is a sombre day for the nation as people gather to mourn and remember the nearly 3,000 victims of the attacks on September 11 2001, when 19 al-Qaida hijackers seized control of four airliners, slamming two of the planes into the World Trade Center, one into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, and the fourth into a field in western Pennsylvania.

We have comprehensive coverage of the anniversary, which will be marked by ceremonies around the world. There are stories of the day from people who were there. Stanley Praimnath and Brian Clark were two of only four individuals known to have survived above the impact zone in the south tower, and
title: Nation pauses to remember September 11 on 25th anniversary | First Thing

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Paul Roberts, who was employed by UPS for 44 years, was working at a customer care center when he was struck

A longtime United Parcel Service (UPS) employee less than two weeks away from retiring was struck and killed by one of the company’s vehicles while he was at work in St Louis, triggering a federal labor investigation along with an intense outpouring of grief from his family and colleagues.

Paul Roberts, 63, was on duty at the UPS customer care center in Earth City, Missouri, on the night of 4 September when a company vehicle hit him, authorities said.

Continue reading...
title: Missouri UPS worker two weeks from retirement fatally struck by company vehicle

author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
description:
Unexpected GDP rise comes as borrowing costs and inflation risks mount ahead of Healey’s first budget

The UK economy grew in July despite the fallout from the Iran war, in welcome news for John Healey ahead of next month’s budget.

Figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed a 0.4% increase in gross domestic product (GDP), compared with 0.3% growth in June.

Continue reading...
title: UK economy defies forecasts with surprise 0.4% growth in July

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Global oil price at its highest since May while investors dump stocks and bonds after Donald Trump’s $5,000 ‘dividend’ promise

Fuel prices are on track to climb a further 20 to 30 cents over coming weeks as the escalating Middle East conflict pushed the global oil price to its highest since mid-May.

As investors dumped stocks and bonds in an increasingly febrile environment, Donald Trump’s promise to give every US adult citizen a $US5,000 “dividend” after the November mid-terms added to alarm around the parlous state of the country’s finances.

Continue reading...
title: Australian fuel prices set to rise by 30c as global markets react to ‘deadly cocktail’

author: Alex Daniel
description:
National Audit Office says failure to implement £70bn modernisation would also hold back economic growth

  • The ‘great grid upgrade’ is off track – ministers should spell out the risks for bills

Consumers will pay higher energy bills unless the UK government speeds up work on a vast programme of upgrades to the electricity grid to enable the switch to renewables, the public spending watchdog has warned.

The National Audit Office (NAO) said that without faster action the extra costs associated with managing the ageing power network, which are ultimately passed on to the public, could reach £7.8bn a year by 2030.

Continue reading...
title: Speed up electricity grid upgrade or else face higher bills, warns UK watchdog

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Trespass case launched by two mothers settled after officers often went to families’ houses between midnight and 4am

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two Indigenous mothers have settled a trespass case against New South Wales police, after officers turned up at one of their homes 150 times in 20 months to conduct bail che
title: NSW police settle trespass case after visiting Indigenous children’s home 150 times in 20 months

author: David Smith in Dallas, Texas
description:
The president demonised Democrats in an attempt to wangle votes in midterms despite backlash over Iran war

With his approval rating at a historic low, Donald Trump has brought down the curtain on the Republicans’ first ever midterm convention by pleading with supporters to do him “the biggest favour” and “pretend” they are voting for him in November’s US elections.

The president is facing a growing backlash over rising prices and the war in Iran. Sweeping losses for the Republican party could effectively turn Trump into a lame duck for his final two years in the White House.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’m on the ticket’: Trump implores Republicans to vote in November at unusual midterm convention

author: Adam Gabbatt in Dallas
description:
Vice-president dog-whistled, exaggerated claims of success and echoed Trump talking points to excited audience

JD Vance made a clear pitch that he should be the heir to Donald Trump on Thursday night, closing out the Republicans’ midterm convention with a blistering speech that featured exaggerated claims of success, criticism of Democrats as “lunatics” and an aggressive dismissal of a protester waving a Mexican flag.

Speaking in Dallas, the vice-president showed he could channel the basest instincts of his boss, filling his remarks with dog whistles and echoing Trump’s false claims that Democrats “cheered” the 7 October massacre of Israelis.

Continue reading...
title: JD Vance pitches himself as Trump’s political heir on day two of Republican midterm convention

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
A split emerges in One Nation over the video, with Barnaby Joyce offering an apology as Pauline Hanson continues to refuse to take it down

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Andrew Hastie has accepted an apology from his former colleague Barnaby Joyce over a One Nation cartoon video labelling the former SAS captain a traitor but reiterated that he believed Pauline Hanson was a “lying coward”.

The apology has revealed a split between Joyce and his leader, as Hanson
title: Hastie accepts apology from Joyce over ‘traitor’ cartoon as Hanson doubles down and tells critics to ‘chill’

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Luke Sayers says he accepts Cate Sayers did not post photo of his genitals as she says settlement closes ‘painful and difficult chapter’

The embattled former AFL club president Luke Sayers has apologised to his former wife for the harm he caused as her defamation case over a lewd photo settled.

Lawyers for Sayers, the immediate past president of the Carlton football club, read out the apology in the Victorian supreme court on Friday after indicating the settlement.

Continue reading...
title: Former Carlton president apologises to ex-wife as lewd photo defamation case settles

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Ticehurst’s former partner had pleaded guilty to stabbing her 15 times at her Forbes home just before midnight on 21 April 2024

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Molly Ticehurst’s ex-boyfriend has been sentenced to 28 years in jail for her senseless and brutal murder, which was revenge for her reporting allegations of sexual assault to police.

Daniel Billings was sentenced in the NSW supreme court in Orange today by Justice Natalie Adams, who imposed a non-parole
title: Molly Ticehurst’s killer Daniel Billings sentenced to 28 years in jail for her murder

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
The flesh-eating parasite had been largely eradicated, but now authorities are racing to contain an outbreak

A horse in southern Texas has been infected with the New World screwworm, marking the first US equine infection as health authorities race to contain an outbreak of the flesh-eating parasite.

The pest was discovered on the hind limb of a working ranch horse in Presidio county, according to a statement on Thursday from US Equestrian Foundation.

Continue reading...
title: Texas reports first equine infection of New World screwworm on ranch horse
